R60 certificates under MAA are scheme A typically. The certificate mentions OIML Issuing Authority NL1 and MAA DoMC — this is the MAA scheme. Given the choices A|B, "A" is appropriate.

Model family: Emax range 2000 kg up to and including 10000 kg. Is this a model family? The characteristics table gives ranges: Emax 2000–10000 kg. It's a range, not discrete models. So probably not a model_family — just type_level characteristics with a range value. The rule says include only if cert covers >1 model variant. There's a range of capacities — could be treated as one type covering capacities 2000-10000 kg. I'll not create model_family; instead type_level max capacity as range {min:2000, max:10000}.

Characteristics (type_level):
- maximum_capacity: {min: 2000, max: 10000}, unit kg
- minimum_dead_load: 0, kg
- accuracy_class: "C" — hmm, string value. Value "C", unit null. Also in recommendation.accuracy_classes: ["C"].
- rated_output: 2.0, mV/V
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: 3000 (label "Maximum number of load cell intervals (n)" → canonical: max_number_of_load_cell_intervals_nlc; the example uses max_load_cell_intervals_nlc)
- ratio_y_emax_over_vmin: 21900 — the label "Ratio of minimum LC Verification interval Y = Emax / vmin". Value 21900.
- ratio_z_emax_over_dr: 4400 — "Ratio of minimum dead load output return Z = Emax / (2 * DR)" → canonical ratio_z... maybe "ratio_z_emax_over_2dr" or "minimum_dead_load_output_return_ratio_z". I'll use ratio_z_emax_over_2dr. Hmm. Rule 1 example: `Ratio of minimum LC Verification interval(1) Y=Emax/vmin` → `ratio_y_emax_over_vmin`. So Z → ratio_z_emax_over_2dr. I'll go with that.
- input_impedance: 1100 Ω ± 50 Ω — this is a nominal with tolerance. Value: could be {min:1050, max:1150} or string "1100 ± 50". Better: value 1100, unit_symbol "Ω", plus separate? Hmm. Simplest: value: {"min": 1050, "max": 1150}, unit_symbol "Ω". Or value: 1100 with tolerance noted... The schema says value can be number | {min,max} | string. I'll use {min: 1050, max: 1150}. Actually, tolerance ±50 implies range. That's reasonable.
- temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C
- apportionment_factor_plc: 0.7
- humidity_class: "CH"
- safe_overload: 200, unit "%" with safe_overload_reference: "Emax" (per rule 3 example). 
- output_impedance: {min: 998, max: 1002}, unit Ω. Or 1000 ± 2.
- recommended_excitation: 10, V (AC/DC → power type). Rule: 110-240V AC 50/60Hz split into voltage, frequency, type. Here "10 V AC / DC" — value 10, unit V, plus type "AC/DC". I could add excitation_type: "AC/DC". Let me do recommended_excitation_voltage: 10 V and recommended_excitation_type: "AC/DC". Hmm, but the label is "Recommended excitation". Simpler: recommended_excitation: {value: 10, unit_symbol: "V"} and separate recommended_excitation_type: "AC / DC". I'll do that.
- excitation_maximum: 15 V → excitation_maximum_voltage: 15 V.
- transducer_material: "Stainless steel"
- atmospheric_protection: "Welded sealing"

Note "The characteristics for nmax and Y can be reduced separately." — a note; could add as description footnote? Not a footnote with marker. Skip or add to description? Schema has no place; maybe ignore.
